speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Affordability can be objectively measured but it is subjectively felt.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is why you cannot soothe emotions using statistics.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My husband and I share household chores as we do not have a helper.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our older resale flat, which we first bought when we got married, is small enough for us to maintain together.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In a hypothetical example, six out of seven days of the week, he will do his part of the chores, but on the one day that he does not, I remember the previous days that he did not.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When he reminds me of his efforts on the six days, I feel frustrated and think about that one day.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, firstly, I would like to thank him for it.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I do not believe it is time to throw the baby out with the bath water.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The HDB was set up during a housing crisis in Singapore in the 1960s.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And over the years, these flats are home to around 80% of our population – around 23 towns and three estates.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must not compare only harking back to the past, but our place vis-à-vis the rest of the world.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Moving on to some suggestions, the two areas of focus I would like to suggest are: policies that boost the resale market viability as housing option for first-time homeowners and policies that focus on increased access to temporary housing for Singaporeans who need to rent, while on their way to becoming homeowners.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We will need some time to see these come into effect.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That alongside the ground structures available, support Singaporeans in our pursuit of purchasing our first home, be it first hand from HDB or in the resale market.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, despite the Government's best efforts in rolling out cooling measures to manage increasing prices in the resale market, sometimes market conditions will cause demand to skyrocket beyond predicted levels, and with it, prices increase.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have some suggestions specific to future BTO projects.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Scenario A: a couple successfully ballots for a 3-room BTO.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They are eligible for an HDB Loan Eligibility (HLE) loan and receive the proximity grant to be near their parents.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lucky for them, three years later, they have a child and feel that maybe their house is a little too cramped as they also are considering employing a foreign domestic worker.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given that they have reached their three-year MOP, the couple contemplate selling their home to purchase a 4-room flat in the resale market to accommodate their growing family.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Scenario B: same couple and choices, except they have not had the fortune to have a child yet.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, in considering their next home purchase, they are not eligible for this stage of life housing grant.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, because they had right-sized at the start, the share of wallet paying their mortgage from their monthly income is slightly lower and they have savings.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They afford this first home comfortably and when their salary scales, they can afford a bigger home, either later down the line or when they have kids.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And the status quo continues to exist for them.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The MOP period will continue to be at five years.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These twin proposals encourage a rethink of how we as Singaporeans approach housing, buying the space that we need today and upgrading as needs change in the future, allowing space and assistance to go to those when you need it the most.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While there will naturally be many considerations in these suggestions, I hope that this concept can be considered and its potentials studied further as one of the many levers which the Ministry uses.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, as a Member of Parliament serving in a mature estate, I often receive feedback that the price of resale units are high.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are few new BTOs and that the younger generation wants to continue to stay in the same neighbourhood and nearer their parents who are part of their circle of care.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My husband and I too, prioritise proximity to my senior parents so that we could be a short distance away if we needed them or if they needed us, even though the trade-off in that was an older flat and an older layout.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would allow both caregiving for children and parents more holistically in a larger space and also free up other units for resale when parents move in together with their children.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Personally, I am grateful that the Government has started to consider prime location public housing and continues to find scarce piece in mature estates instead of such land being taken up by private housing only.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   There are around 50,000 households under the Public Rental Scheme.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In 2022, the Government stated that the waiting period to get a rental flat from HDB is less than one year.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is lower than countries like Hong Kong, for example, where the waiting period for public housing is 5.6 years.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, many of my residents have shared their concerns – for example, a mother and her children who suddenly lost their home after a divorce and those living in 1-room rental flats, which is not suitable for children who are growing up.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Sometimes there are also complex issues faced by families such as families that have recently reconciled or those with new family members at home such as in-laws.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such vouchers can complement the support provided by the Government to address the rental flat supply problem and can provide a quicker solution to a most pressing need.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, this policy, if approved, should have a testing method and eligibility criteria such as an income limit, a maximum limit on the amount to be drawn out and consider whether it is appropriate for the Government to provide a repository of homeowners with additional rooms.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my view, such housing vouchers can provide more support for low-income Singaporeans and alleviate situations where there are no units available for them to rent.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It also allows families to rent in locations closer to schools, workplaces or family support systems that they require.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Home Ownership Support Team (HST), coupled with the Fresh Start Housing Scheme (FSHS), has helped them.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mortgage rates have doubled on average in developed countries in 2022.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, in Indonesia, a 2019 World Bank report on urbanisation, showed that the ratio of home prices to income in Jakarta was higher than Singapore and New York City, and this led to a reduction in home ownership rate.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In Malaysia, a policy paper has suggested that housing prices remain unaffordable for many residents.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Housing is a global problem, but remains a personal aspiration for many, and we must continue to improve accessibility and affordability for current and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Madam, our housing policy approach has historically gone beyond infrastructure to include livability, social, familial and societal development considerations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have worked so hard for generations of Singaporeans to own houses and build homes.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And as we navigate new expectations and realities, I hope that the Government continues to listen to concerns as it has and also be open in communicating trade-offs so our people understand the different data points when discussing affordability and accessibility in housing.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Just to give the background as how I came to that conclusion and to clarify.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And, that it would eventually have to be paid back to the past reserves.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: Whether it is now or whether it is later, it is still part.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: The land cost is still now part of the pricing of the HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: And when a person purchases flat, surely, they will look at what this land cost is and consider it because it is a future liability.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, the cost of the land is in fact, not out of the picture in this new proposal.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: It is, in fact, now in the picture, squarely in the picture, although it maybe in the background.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: So, this is the reason why I came to the conclusion that there were actually differences in what he had proposed earlier and what he is proposing now because it has quite obviously changed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If I am a military strategist, obviously, I have just executed a very brilliant strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Since the earliest days of nation-building, home ownership has been a key cornerstone of our public housing policy and a key pillar of Singapore's social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As a young nation, we want to support all Singaporeans to own their own homes, so that they can have stability to build their families and raise their children, have a sense of rootedness in Singapore, and have a stake in our country's progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have one of the highest home ownership rates in the world, at close to 90%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many Singaporeans have also benefited from the growth in the value of their HDB flats and upgraded to new homes at different stages of their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government's commitment to help Singaporeans own their own homes remain firm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Virtually all first-time buyers of subsidized flats get to select a flat within three tries if they apply for BTO flats in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Overall, almost nine in 10 first-time BTO buyers in non-mature estates can finance their monthly HDB housing loan fully with CPF, without any cash.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Moving forward, like what we have done before, we will continue to ensure that public housing is accessible and affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also take care of the housing needs of those who are more vulnerable and lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Madam, I will continue my speech in English, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As Minister Desmond Lee said in his speech, one of the Government's key objectives is to create an inclusive society, through public housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is why our housing grants are tiered to provide more support for lower-income families, on top of the significant subsidies provided for BTO flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As a result, about 85% of our low-income households own their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is something not commonly seen in other countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Take for example, a lower-income family with household income of $2,500, which is below the second decile of resident household income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This family would only need to use about 16% of their household income for their monthly mortgage instalments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This means they can service their mortgage entirely using their monthly CPF contributions, without any cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Or if you look at a household combined income of $5,000, which is below the third decile of resident household income, they can receive $45,000 in housing grants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Based on a typical selling price of $350,000 for a 4-room flat in West Glade @ Bukit Batok in the November 2022 BTO exercise, the housing grant can reduce the selling price to $305,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This family would only need to use about 21% of their household income to pay for their monthly mortgage instalments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Again, they can service their mortgages entirely from their monthly CPF contributions, with no cash outlay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As these examples show, HDB flats continue to remain affordable, even for families on the lower end of the income range.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond delivering our commitment to affordable and accessible public housing, we have been going all out to take care of those who are more vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We recognise that some families may not be ready for home ownership yet as they need to build up their finances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To ensure that these families and their children have a stable home as they work on their life challenges, we provide highly subsidised public rental housing as a social safety net.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been making improvements to our rental flats over the years to provide a better living environment for our tenants and we will continue to do more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, we improved the design so newer rental blocks have better lighting and ventilation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: And going forward, we will be building rental blocks in the same projects as sold blocks and where possible, in the same block.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Doing so also helps to ensure that our HDB estates remain inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For low-income singles in public rental flats who are under the Joint Single Scheme, or JSS, we know that some of them have difficulties finding a flatmate or getting along with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A few years back, we started building partitioned 1-room flats for the JSS, to provide more privacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More recently, we started piloting an operator-run model for the JSS, where we appoint an operator to help manage the flat-sharing arrangements, and individuals can apply without having to find a flat-mate first.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These efforts have been well received so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For our rental tenants, our approach goes beyond providing rental flats for shelter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to ensure that their children have a stable home environment to grow up in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ComLink officers will work with the families to understand their needs and aspirations, then develop customised goals and an action plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Depending on their needs, we bring in the relevant support schemes and programmes across the various agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, ComCare financial assistance, employment support for the parents, and KidSTART for the children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For rental families who have achieved stability and have potential for home ownership, we set up the Home ownership Support Team, or HST in short, in HDB to journey with them through their flat-buying process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The HST provides one-to-one guidance to help families work out their budget, make sense of the housing grants and schemes available, all the way until they move into their new flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I work with them very closely and we engage rental tenants, as well as those who have moved into their new flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I have met some families who have benefited from HST's guidance and they are always very appreciative of the effort that our HST officers put in to help them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, I met a young couple last September, Nizam and Nabilah, who had just moved into their new home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Before that, they had lived in a public rental flat for some years with their three young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From the outset, they were determined to work towards home ownership to provide a better home environment for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Knowing that steady income with CPF contribution is crucial, both of them persevered in their jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Nabilah shared with me that their journey was not without challenges, but they were determined and worked hard to save up for their own flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As they were not sure about their housing budget, they sought help from the HST.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The HST worked with the family to plan their housing budget and options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They also benefited from an Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of $60,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They are now the proud owners of a beautiful 4-room flat in Punggol.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact, I visited them at their home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some of our rental families are those who had to move into public rental housing after losing their flat due to financial difficulties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To help these second-timer families with children own a home again, we introduced the Fresh Start Housing Scheme (Fresh Start).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under Fresh Start, they can buy a shorter-lease 2-room Flexi flat with a grant and receive support from a Social Service Agency (SSA) to help them stay on track in their journey towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of our Fresh Start families is Mdm Zaidah and her son.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After eight years in public rental housing, she bought a Fresh Start flat three years ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: When she was interviewed recently, Mdm Zaidah said, "My son and I are so happy to have our very own home." Simple words, but there is so much behind it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: She has brought up three children, gone through divorce, and battled cancer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Now, she has her own flat – a home for life, paid for in full with her CPF savings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In guiding her towards home ownership, we have been very inspired by her and we are so happy for her too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I was very happy to read Mdm Zaidah's interview.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I could resonate with her happiness, particularly that of her son, as that was how my family, particularly my siblings and I, felt in 1979 when we moved from a rental flat in Marine Terrace to our 3-room flat in Bedok South.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I sat down reflecting and appreciating what we have here in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I told myself I knew how she felt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We must do more to help fellow Singaporeans, especially those who live in rental flats to have a home of their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are very encouraged by this, as it shows that home ownership is achievable for our rental families, with hard work and commitment on their part, coupled with strong support from the Government and the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As part of building an inclusive society, we have also adjusted our policies to take care of those who may be facing housing challenges due to unexpected life events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Especially when children are involved, we want to ensure that they can have a stable home to grow up in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those going through divorce, we understand that the housing transition is a stressful period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For divorced parents with children, I would like to assure them that they can qualify for the same housing schemes and grants as other families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can buy a subsidised flat from HDB or a resale flat on the open market, and qualify for housing grants and priority schemes for families, such as the Multi-Generation Priority Scheme and the Third Child Priority Scheme, if they meet the prevailing eligibility conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To further improve their chances of getting a subsidised flat, those who are buying a flat as second-timers can receive priority under the ASSIST scheme when they apply for a 2-room Flexi or 3-room BTO flat in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those who are undergoing divorce and want to better understand their post-divorce housing options, they can approach HDB for housing counselling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For single unwed parents, if they are in stable employment and can afford to buy a flat, we will allow them to buy up to a 3-room new flat in a non-mature estate, or any resale flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If they cannot afford to buy a flat and need a place to stay, we will consider them for public rental if it is in the best interest of their child, in consultation with social workers if necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some Members in this House claimed that seniors will have a lot to worry, when their leases diminish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We take care of our seniors and we have been doing so all along.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, we have planned ahead and introduced measures to help seniors age in place independently and confidently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As part of our neighbourhood upgrading programmes, we have also been adding senior-friendly features to our HDB estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have launched two CCA pilot projects so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The public response has been positive, and we are studying the feedback received as we develop our longer-term plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The CCAs, along with 2-room Flexi flats on shorter leases, also provide right-sizing options for seniors who wish to right-size to a smaller flat after their children move out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue taking care of our seniors’ housing needs, as we have always done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, Madam, to sum up, the Government has delivered on its commitment to affordable and accessible public housing for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To ensure that no one falls through the cracks, we have also gone all out to help those who are more vulnerable and partner them as they work towards a brighter future for themselves and their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue striving to do better as we work with Singaporeans to build an endearing, inclusive home for us and our future generations.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Singapore has one of the highest rates of home ownership in the world, proving that HDB policies have been working well over the generations.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Of course, these housing measures have to evolve to adapt to changing needs.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have done so before and must continue with our efforts to adjust our housing policies to suit new population requirements and social norms.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is important for our HDB flats to be more accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will naturally increase the supply of flats in the market to alleviate supply and demand pressures, First and foremost, it will moderate price increases as the competition for resale flats is lowered.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, it will allow better family planning for couples who prefer to have their own homes before starting a family.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I appeal to the Ministry to provide further priority for first timers who need their flats more urgently.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These include married couples trying for a child and those with young children.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB may need to look into their family situation, such as proximity to the parents' home, the couple's age, number of unsuccessful HDB applications and allocate higher priority.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Supposing we are able to improve the supply situation, the question of affordability is also top on the minds of flat buyers.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB has done well over the years to ensure availability of a good mix of different flat types in a wide range of prices.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Together with the relevance of subsidies and assistance schemes, home ownership is within reach for a broad spectrum of budgets.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, there will be a group of applicants who need or want to stay close to the parents but are worried about whether the prices of BTO flats in these areas are within their budget, especially if their parents are residing in matured states, which command level of pricing that is on the higher range due to their prime or central location.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How do we create a situation where we can achieve a good outcome for this group of applicants?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To maintain a fair market, HDB would have to differentiate pricing of flats according to their location in line with how real estate is priced.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While bridging the aspirations of multi-generational families who want to stay in close proximity, we also need to be cognizant of market forces at play as HDB flats are also bought and sold on the secondary market.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Increasing supply of BTO flats indiscriminately and skewing pricing to the low end would create downward pressure under the resale HDB flat market and impact existing home owners.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Aside from the forces of supply and demand and location, the lease tenure of a property would also be a factor in his pricing or value.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: A debate on the Motion on providing affordable and accessible public housing for Singaporeans must look at the past, the present and the future, keeping in focus members of the older generation, current generation and future generations.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The provision of public housing has to be seen in the historical context of both tackling the challenges of providing good jobs for a newly independent country suffering high unemployment as well as forming a nation.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Having a place called home produces a sense of belonging.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: What has been the record of the Government in achieving this goal over the past few decades?

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: As the standard of living has risen and citizens' aspirations have evolved, what are the challenges to the Government commitment to provide affordable and accessible housing to the cross section of the current generation?

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: If we attach a positive weight to the social welfare of future generations, how should we view and seek to meet the housing needs?

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In the report of Singapore Housing Committee 1947, it was noted that the lack of proper housing posed a serious problem.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I quote: "These people live in huts made of atap, old boxes, rusty corrugated iron, etc., with no sanitation, water or any of the elementary health requirements.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: It is a literal and physical impossibility to eject these people as they have at present nowhere else to go and cannot be cramped back into the slums from which they have escaped." The report expressed an aspiration to build permanent housing over a period of 25 years.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: While the Singapore Improvement Trust established by the colonial administration started to build houses to meet the challenges described in the 1947 report, the take-off began only with the establishment of the HDB after Singapore achieved self-government in 1959.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In the book titled "First decade in public housing, 1960 to 1969", the then-Minister for Law and National Development, EW Barker, said in his foreword, and I quote: "One of the more glaring problems that the government inherited when it was elected to office in 1959 was the acute shortage of housing.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: A large proportion of the population was then living in squalid dwellings, concentrated mainly in the city.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Whatever little accommodation that was available on the market with a modicum of comfort and modern conveniences was beyond the reach of the majority of the people.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: This makes keeping a job that pays reasonably well a prerequisite to owning a home.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The unemployment rate steadily declined, from close to 9% while real income saw a steady rise after Singapore became independent in 1965.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Members of the Pioneer Generation made difficult adjustments as they transited from living in attap huts to living in HDB flats.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew in his memoir entitled "From Third World to First: The Singapore Story: 1965-2000" told of a family – a couple of 12 children – moving from a hut to a new HDB flat at Old Airport Road, they brought a dozen chickens and ducks to rear in the kitchen.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Members of the Pioneer Generation and their children, including members of the Merdeka Generation, also benefited, looking at the past generation, from the appreciation of the value of their flats as real income rose steadily during the period of what I like to call catch-up growth.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: It is very likely that economic growth itself, particularly equitable growth that distributed benefits to different segments of the resident population, which Singapore experienced, served to enhance the value of a home.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, the rise in the value of a home in general, broadly speaking, on average, occurred because of the great transition from a third world to a first, signifying a closing of the income gap between Singapore in 1965 to the world economic leader of the 20th century.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, the constant effort to refresh HDB estates, including mature estates, also helps in asset enhancement.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Take the example of a member of the Pioneer Generation whose age was in the early forties during the late 1970s.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: That would have been about the time when the Pioneer Generation moved from the attap huts to their first HDB flats.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: When such a member in their early forties, during the late 1970s, purchased a HDB flat, he did that with a 99-year lease.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In his eighties today, he can, through joint ownership, leave his HDB flat with a remaining lease of still over 50 years as a bequest to one of his children.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Those with children, some of whom might be members of the Merdeka Generation who choose to purchase their own BTO or resale flat, have, as Members have noted, the following options.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: These are means to monetise their housing asset and boost retirement adequacy.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: What are the challenges to providing affordable housing to the cross-section of the current generation?

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: As has been noted, the Government has made clear that keeping public housing affordable to help Singaporeans own their homes is a key national priority.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In that regard, two measures are regularly used in international studies.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The BTO flats are priced to maintain a certain price-to-income ratio (PIR), taking into account the different locational and individual attributes of BTO flats.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Housing subsidies given to Singaporeans purchasing their first flat bring down the PIR compared to the higher PIR for resale flats in the same locality.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: This makes it possible for most flat buyers, in the example just given, to service their loan without further cash outlays.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: They can simply draw down their CPF contributions.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The supply of BTO flats has been disrupted due to COVID-19.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I think many Members have recognised that among different factors, this was probably a major shock, increasing the waiting time to get one's first BTO flat.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: But the pace of construction has resumed and some time will be taken before the market adjusts to an equilibrium to match supply to demand.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: However, I think it is important to understand the nature of the market equilibrium under a BTO system.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: When demand is high relative to supply, as we are facing now, an unfettered price mechanism would allocate goods to final users basically by driving up the price.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Since the Government seeks to make public housing affordable by achieving a certain price-to-income ratio, the allocation therefore is achieved through balloting.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: For example, this means that individual preferences for certain flat types might not be met, especially when there is a desire to have a BTO flat in a mature estate, say, for reasons of closer proximity to parents who can help to provide childcare for working couples.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Since the physical capacity to build BTO flats in mature estates is much more limited, the Government might have to consider more childcare facilities in non-mature estates to shift housing preferences.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Despite broadly equitable growth that very much characterised the Singapore experience through the second half of the 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, from around the year 2000, while the real wage of high-skilled workers continued to rise, that of low-skilled workers remained fairly stagnant.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, it slightly declined from about year 2000.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: As a portion of the Workfare payments is given in the form of CPF top ups, this helps to build up retirement adequacy.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, there are national policies other than monetising assets, as long-term structural policies that boost retirement adequacy, almost surely, this will have to be a major form as we proceed in the decades ahead because the experience from developed countries has shown that in more recent decades, wage inequality has indeed widened.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: As has been noted, households at the lower end of the income distribution receive additional grants to purchase their HDB flats, enabling them to have access to public housing and thus become owners also of an important asset.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The size of their enhanced CPF housing grant is graduated to give a higher amount to lower-income earners.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: So, I think I have now made broadly two points.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I think that it is fairly undeniable that if you look at a country like Singapore, certainly, its prospects and its independence, few would have figured that it could transit from about 20% of the US standard of living to having caught up.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I think that a central part of that growth is associated with the increase in the value of housing.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: But to have a house, you have got to have a job, which makes CPF and employability, a point that I will conclude with, very crucial.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: It is Singapore's ability to generate both the jobs and, of course, along with that, reasonably good pay that force us now to widen the income inequality gap.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I think the social consensus is to have special policies, especially to uplift the earnings of low-wage workers, and to have a policy where we have tiered external grants that are in their favour.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I think point number two is that the success of meeting current aspirations, in part, will involve refinements – not a total change.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I want to address here the issue of the value of land and placing it into the reserves and give a perspective on that.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: The proceeds, as is the current practice, from land purchases by HDB are ploughed back into the past reserves.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Valuing land and market rates and paying into the past reserves generate resources to tackle negative external shocks and boost employment for current and future generations.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, as we have seen recently from the COVID-19 pandemic shock as well as earlier episodes of recessionary shock such as the Global Financial Crisis, keeping a job is not guaranteed as a matter of course.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Avoiding long periods of unemployment enabled Singaporeans to continue contributing to their CPF accounts to finance their mortgages.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: So, augmenting our past reserves by channelling proceeds from land sales by HDB at market rates therefore serves to increase the country's resources for use during stormy days.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: In the absence of any housing grants that are financed through current tax revenues, HDB would not have the proceeds to plough back to past reserves as it currently does.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Past reserves would therefore not accumulate at the same rate as under the current system.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: Under the proposed scheme, the purchasers of BTO flats who, for various reasons, choose to sell in the resale market would have to pay the apportioned land cost with accrued interest that will be added to past reserves.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: It details the before and the after of a typical living room and a kitchen.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
text: I am old enough to have seen how an attap hut looks like – a kitchen in the attap hut looks very different from a kitchen in the HDB flat —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Prof Hoon Hian Teck, I am sorry to interrupt you, but you have a minute and a half to close.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck
text: Living through the rapid economic transformation of Singapore leaves one with a deep sense of gratitude.

speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck
text: I support the Motion standing in the name of the Minister for National Development.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Muhammad Faishal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, as I have shared in my speech, this is not something that we have recently done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is something that we have journeyed through for many years, and we have always been doing this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if you see, how it has transformed from the 2-room Flexi flats and we have now started to embark on the Community Care Apartments (CCAs).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We look at ageing and also looking after the needs of the seniors, not only from the aspect of housing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is a comprehensive plan that involves not only multi-disciplinary, multi-Ministries, but I think various segments of our people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But there is an opportunity for us to provide the platforms for our people to age gracefully, age in place and find joy in ageing here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have journeyed through many years before, even decades.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, I realise that the landscape continues to change and there are developments, for example, in technology, and how we can provide social services, healthcare services together, and we want to have better integration that will help them in their lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And not only that, to also help their family members and their children to support them, so that we all can grow well in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I assure the Member that this is something that we are looking at.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have been looking at it and we continue to look at it, to find ways on how we can integrate and provide a holistic move in developments towards ageing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee's opening speech gave an overview of how we have been building and pricing HDB flats, explained the causes for the current tightness in the supply of BTO flats and higher prices in the resale market, laid out the moves we are making to address the situation and reaffirmed the Government's commitment of keeping public housing affordable and accessible, while protecting the interest of current and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is natural to adjust public housing policy from time to time, in response to changes in demand, societal trends, buyer expectations and major events with profound impact on the housing market, such as the Asian Financial Crisis in the past and the COVID-19 pandemic which we have so recently experienced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But to require a reset, as the Member Mr Leong Mun Wai has claimed, is something else altogether.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members would recall the points that Minister Desmond Lee has made yesterday.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In his opening speech, he has given us some handouts, which I trust that Members have saved because they are very useful, but if not, we have made extra copies available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In his speech, he showed that we have been building HDB flats faster than the HDB residential population growth – and that is in Annex 1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Median household income growth grew faster than the increase in average 4-room BTO prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And this, Members can see from Annex 7.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB has also kept to our affordability targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More than eight in 10 buyers who collected their keys to BTO flats or bought resale flats in 2022, can service their monthly mortgage fully from CPF contributions, with little to no cash outlay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For first-timers who apply for BTO flats in non-mature estates, virtually everyone gets a chance to select a flat within three tries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee's presentation has shown how, over the long term, we have not underbuilt BTOs nor have we lost sight of affordability, especially for non-mature estate BTOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree with Members' observations about short-term imbalances in supply and the spike in resale price levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Not only did Minister Desmond Lee lay out the causes, he also explained what we are doing about these imbalances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the median, but even if we look at the range, it is not the five to seven years that Mr Leong mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is more like two to six years and the BTO project with the longest waiting time today is an almost 50-storey development at just under six years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Resale prices have, indeed, grown more sharply recently, due to buyers turning to resale when BTO construction was delayed due to COVID-19, and shifts in social norms exacerbated by the experience of the pandemic, contributing to overall increase in housing demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Cooling measures have been introduced, which are starting to take effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mature estate BTOs present a specific set of concerns which Minister Desmond has also addressed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These mature estate BTOs are in desirable locations and cannot possibly be priced the same as other locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Nominated Member Cheng Hsing Yao has alluded to, mature estate BTOs are really more than basic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Although some prospective buyers find them pricey, there are still many buyers within the eligible income range who are able and willing to pay the posted price, as can be seen by the high application rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The issue is how to price mature estate BTOs, so that they do not become out of reach for most buyers, and also not in a way that induces its own demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Desmond Lee has also indicated new measures we are considering to manage demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So he has laid out the long-term picture and he has also addressed the short-term imbalances and what we are going to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And in the speeches that have followed, I was very glad to see considerable common ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, Members like Mr Gerald Giam and Mr Leon Perera have also agreed that building more flats with short waiting times and also efforts to manage demand are important – and this is what we are doing or considering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Nominated Member Dr Shahira Abdullah has also raised suggestions for managing demand amongst BTO buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We thank her also for agreeing with us that these are important issues to consider.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members have also made suggestions that affirm the need to make sure that resale prices are moderated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But this means ensuring that the price increases are sustainable and will not crash or be very volatile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And again, I think that we are in agreement here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, if we agree that the imbalances that Minister Desmond Lee has laid out are the challenges facing us, then Mr Leong's proposal of the Affordability Housing Scheme (AHS) does not quite solve any of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: His scheme also raises more questions than it answers, as many Members, including Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Raj Joshua Thomas, Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Lim Biow Chuan have been quick to point out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I do not wish to recap too much of the scheme, because I think many Members have done so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Suffice to say, that the scheme has attracted much comment, and yet, I think it has also perplexed commentators, because it is not so clear whether it really will be attractive to applicants or not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And if it is attractive to applicants, I think that commentators see problems and if it is not attractive to applicants, I think there are also problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, for instance, if there are a lot of applicants, then perhaps, they are attracted by the super low price upon entry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, there is also a very high clawback consisting of the land cost if they wish to sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And at the point of entry, because if the low prices really do attract applicants, we can imagine that it will also attract many applicants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But if there is a lot of demand, then does that not make it harder for first-timers to get a flat?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And does that not worsen the current concerns that some have about accessibility?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And for those who may wish to one day sell, because the clawback is very large, and as Members have pointed out, this is a clawback on a cost base model, not the affordability model that we currently price BTOs on – so, it is possible that prospective sellers of these flats are actually looking at a much higher price that they have to pay to the Government, if you add everything up together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, a paradoxical feature of this scheme is that you buy when you sell, or you sell when you buy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If they are not able to muster the financial resources to sell, then what are their options?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What does this mean for those who actually do want to exit, or they want to upgrade, or move somewhere else?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Are they able to find buyers who are willing to pay a very high price?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And also, should there be strong demand amongst applicants, Members have also pointed out the implications of upheaval in the resale market and they are concerned that the value of existing home owners' assets would also be negatively impacted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is if the scheme is attractive to applicants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the scheme is not attractive to applicants, also for the reasons that commentators have pointed out, I think that is also a concern, because then would that not mean that, young people included, applicants would abandon the public housing scheme?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And how is that also better for Singapore on the whole?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, that is probably enough said about the perplexing nature of the BTO pricing scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I think it is important to also address another prominent element in it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under the scheme, the land cost is not paid if the applicant or the person does not sell the flat, but this is a draw on reserves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, from the get-go, we can think of the scheme as a prepaid rental scheme leveraged on past reserves, because as long as the person is living in the flat and he is not selling it, he is not able to realise any gains or any value, and it does not seem that he has the rights of ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Although we call it public housing, the use of the flat is exclusive to the household that owns it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And this is completely different from public infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More importantly, HDB flat owners can sell their flats if they wish, and keep the proceeds, but we cannot break public infrastructure up, sell it off and pocket the proceeds as individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The "Millenial Apartments Scheme" to appeal to young people who are not yet ready to buy their own HDB flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Louis Chua and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim have made similar points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has heard a range of suggestions in our Forward Singapore conversations and we will be studying them and some of these suggestions also relate to similar ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Home ownership remains an important goal of public housing as it gives Singaporeans a tangible stake in nation-building and also boosts their financial security, especially in retirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Paid rent, even if subsidised, is a consumption expense that could have gone towards financing home purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And compared to subsidising rental as a lifestyle, subsidising home ownership brings more benefits, especially if it is for the majority of Singaporeans for whom home ownership is attainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PSP and WP Members, who have spoken on their concerns about retirement adequacy, ought to appreciate how having one’s own home protects us against the uncertainties of the rental market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will speak a little bit more about that later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And we are doing our utmost to ensure BTO flats continue to be accessible and affordable to younger buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Several Members have identified resale prices as a concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And here, I wish to make a distinction between the long-term trend in resale prices and the short-term spike that occurred during the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Resale prices have moved up over the long term, certainly more than BTO prices have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is because we changed the basis of calculating HDB loans since 1993.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a good thing for HDB home owners, because they would otherwise not be able to benefit from the fully realised market value of their flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the long term, resale prices reflect broad economic conditions and income levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ideally, prices should be stable, with as few sharp fluctuations as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that some first-timers do turn to the resale market instead of buying direct from HDB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And this is why the Government provides grants to make resale flats more affordable to eligible buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We believe this approach is fair to both sellers and buyers – allowing homeowners to enjoy the full value of their asset and yet also giving some help to buyers to bridge the affordability gap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These points I have made about resale are relevant to my next topic, a concern that the PSP’s curious BTO pricing proposal is purported to resolve and that is liberating more CPF from being deployed for housing purchase, and thereby improving retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The PSP claims that as the value of a home owner’s flat falls as the lease diminishes, and since much of his CPF savings had been used towards the flat’s purchase, retirement adequacy is at risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And Assoc Prof Jamus Lim appears to share similar thoughts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This claim is flawed and has to be clarified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Helping Singaporeans achieve home ownership and retirement adequacy are both important goals for the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, our CPF and HDB policies are closely inter-linked.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Owning a HDB flat that can last us for life is, in itself, important for retirement security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Because the retiree would be assured of a home without having to rent accommodation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The flat could potentially also be monetised to supplement living expenses, through renting out a room, the whole flat, or through the Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And this is why we allow the use of the CPF Ordinary Account (OA) towards housing purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But we do not depend on home ownership alone for retirement needs and this is why CPF policy is also focused on helping individuals secure a lifelong cash payout through CPF LIFE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: CPF monies cannot be channelled wholly into housing purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Your Special Account (SA) is safeguarded, and as you grow older, more of your CPF contributions will need to go to SA rather than OA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is also a limit to how much you can draw on the OA for your HDB loan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For BTO flat owners who took HDB loans, HDB does encourage those who have the means and are able to do so, to make early repayments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The earlier they repay the loan, the more they can save on the accrued interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Leong advocates for Singaporeans having the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) in CPF without having to downgrade or sell part of their lease to the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And that is without having to right-size or monetise their HDB flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Of the remaining two in 10, a significant proportion will be expected to accrue additional contributions through employment from age 55 so that they could receive similar payouts at age 65 as those who set aside the cohort BRS when they were at age 55.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many seniors also receive additional retirement support from their loved ones and from their private savings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For members with less in retirement, the Government can provide additional support, such as the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I should add that individual prudence in housing choice is also relevant here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: CPF Members who choose not to max out their OA use towards housing purchase and thus set aside more savings for retirement can look forward to higher CPF LIFE payouts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim expressed concern about the scenario where a home owner has bought a lease that he is likely to outlive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has already considered this possibility and put in place safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Having a lease that lasts the buyer till age 95 is also a condition for withdrawing CPF savings above the BRS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, we have policies in place to safeguard Singaporeans’ retirement adequacy, which do not rely on whether the value of their flat holds or appreciates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Still, I can sense a conundrum behind some of the speeches that Members have made, which is how do we reconcile the phenomenon of appreciating flat values with the fact of eventual lease expiry?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Yesterday, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim provided a handout showing how the value of a HDB flat with 94 years left on the lease would gradually rise and then decline from 2023 to 2116.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He acknowledged the effect of inflation, but he left out the impact of strong economic fundamentals and rising incomes on the value of our flat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Well, unity, hard work and good policies would help to continue creating favourable economic conditions for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Now that our economy is more mature, growth rates cannot be as fast as in the past, but we still work towards delivering a better life for Singaporeans, which would include improvement in incomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Getting this right would mean that the value of this flat would continue rising for a considerable time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, on Assoc Prof Jamus Lim’s chart, the trajectory of value appreciation continues, I believe, for more than 60 of the 94 years, before it begins to fall beyond its original value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our policies allow this buyer to fully realise the value should he chose to monetise by selling – which would not be possible if we mistakenly view rising resale prices as a bad thing to be curbed at all cost.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time our policies are also flexible in providing monetisation options while ageing in place, such as through renting out rooms or Lease Buyback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the reason why although the value of the flat must go to zero after 99 years, that same flat can be a good store of value over a buyer’s lifetime, over the owner's lifetime, and possibly more – so even his children might benefit to some extent – just not over his grandchildren’s lifetimes as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But his children and grandchildren will get Government support in turn to buy their own HDB flats and benefit from having a tangible stake that also appreciates in value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, I hope this reassures Singaporeans who are worried about claims that they will be stuck without recourse when the lease of the flat they bought expires on them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Which brings me to a favourite theme of Mr Leong’s – SERS, VERS and trying to make Singaporeans unhappy over the plain truth that 99 years is 99 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He has not forgotten to riff on this theme during this debate too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I have explained how HDB flats hold their value well and can even appreciate over the owner’s lifetime, albeit not necessarily the entirety of his children’s lifetimes and certainly not his grandchildren’s lifetimes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has been upfront about this with Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is Mr Leong who has been creating ungrounded expectations by trying to convince Singaporeans that it ought to cost them little or nothing to extend the length and value of their leases when it approaches zero.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is the benchmark by which he has been judging SERS and VERS, and unfairly too, because that is simply not their purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If market valuation does not deliver the windfall outcome that Mr Leong so celebrates, then who will deliver it?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It becomes a cost that taxpayers should bear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is something which Mr Murali Pillai has also pointed out yesterday.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
