text: Mr Leong does not acknowledge that what he is encouraging Singaporeans to expect would create an extended benefit that lasts indefinitely over generations, nor does he explain how this is fair.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our policies already equip every generation with the opportunity to own homes and benefit for more than one lifetime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The fair and sustainable thing to do would be for land and buildings to be redeveloped after lease expiry, so that a new generation of Singaporeans can have the same opportunities too, whether or not they were lucky enough to inherit advantages from their parents and grandparents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Leon Perera and also, I believe, yesterday, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim have put forth this suggestion that perhaps the HPI for non-mature estate 4-room flats should be three, that is, an HPI of three and not an HPI of five.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is another one, which in fact just now Prof Hoon Hian Teck alluded to – which is the mortgage servicing ratio or MSR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This, we believe, is also a very good complementary affordability target, particularly because it demonstrates the unique benefits of our CPF system when it works in tandem with our housing policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, let us address his question of whether the HPI should be five or four or three because I believe it was the subject of some lively back and forth earlier in the day between I believe Mr Leon Perera and Mr Xie Yao Quan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I think whether or not the HPI should be four or three, as long as the current target is about five, I think any number that is below five must look attractive to buyers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But, of course, there will be some trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I think it is also in the spirit of what Workers' Party Members have mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are concerned about fiscal sustainability, that we also consider some trade-offs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fact, in the spirit of leaving no stones unturned, this is also a question that my colleagues and I have been asking ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What would it take to bring the HPI down, say, to three?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is an estimated fiscal cost because additional subsidies would be required in order to make this happen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This would be the equivalent of about 20% of our annual healthcare expenditure or about one third of what we spend annually on general education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, housing policies and home prices are hot topics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There has been much discussion and varied viewpoints among the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This Parliamentary debate provides some opportunities for us to clarify public discourse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, has our public housing policy gone terribly wrong?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Has it veered from its mission, requiring a full reset?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is PSP Member Mr Leong Mun Wai's point of view.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our building programme was suspended at one point due to COVID-19, resulting in a short-term crunch in the supply of new flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many home-buyers turned to the resale market and with shifts in the demand for living spaces during the pandemic, we saw a simultaneous increase in demand for both BTO and resale flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MND and HDB have been working on increasing supply and moderating demand, to restore balance and stability in the market as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In his speech, Mr Leong was not able to substantiate his view that public housing policy has gone terribly wrong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He also suggested disregarding land costs so as to sharply reduce the prices of new flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If one plans to sell his flat in the open market, he will have to refund the land cost to the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This suggestion does not address objective reality and hence offers no solution to current issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Not only does it do nothing to relieve the current shortage in housing supply, it may in fact trigger further demand, and can cause serious impact on resale prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Furthermore, the plan contradicts itself in places, resulting in many doubts raised by Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, are Singaporeans over-committing their CPF towards housing?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If flats are not able to hold their value and if homeowners are not able to fully refund their CPF account after selling their flats, would it mean that CPF members have lost out?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Is this not an argument for drastically reducing housing prices?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The handout which Mr Leong distributed in Parliament yesterday propagates this spurious argument.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not how we should be looking at this issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CPF system was designed to support home ownership as well as provide lifelong monthly payouts at old age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why other than the Ordinary Account which can be used for housing purchase, we have the Special Account and Retirement Account which cannot be used for housing purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, there are limits on how much Ordinary Account savings can be used towards housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Having a flat of one's own has a positive impact on retirement security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, the amount of CPF used towards housing purchase would not be in vain, regardless of whether the value of the flat goes up or down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With a home of our own, we no longer have to worry about renting accommodation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When necessary, one can monetise by renting out a room or tap on the Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For members with low CPF balances, the Government can provide support through other assistance schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Of course, we should be prudent when making a home purchase and have a good understanding of the trade-offs involved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If our attitude towards CPF is to "use as much as we can", then naturally we will have less in our CPF account and our monthly CPF LIFE payout in future will be correspondingly lower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Whichever the case may be, we should not perceive our CPF as "suffering a loss" because of home purchase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, while a HDB flat may continue appreciating in value over the years, what should the homeowner do when the 99-year lease expires and value inevitably becomes zero?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Is it the case that the only acceptable solution is to conjure up a large compensation sum for the flat owner to buy a brand new flat?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the political issue that Mr Leong Mun Wai has been enthusiastically stirring up, with the intent of making people anxious and unhappy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over this long period of time, his flat value is very likely to keep appreciating for considerable length of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: WP Member Jamus Lim shared a chart based on his own calculations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He cited a flat with a remaining lease of 94 years as an example and assessed that this flat will appreciate for more than 60 years before dropping in value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the buyer bought the flat at the age of 30, over the course of his lifetime, the value of this flat will go up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If his child lives in the flat with him, then the child would witness the growth in the value of his parents' flat over the decades while growing up, and for some of his adult years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The child would have aged by the time the value of the flat started to depreciate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Member Jamus Lim said this is due to inflation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Actually, he omitted a few important factors, mainly good economic conditions and rising incomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If we stay united, support sound, rational policies and work hard, we can continue to create favourable economic conditions and pursue better incomes for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: By the way, what about cases where the flat owner outlives the 99-year lease of his flat?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, the debate thus far has been helpful in drawing out views that are on the minds of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: With your indulgence, if I may just have half a minute because I was at a Meet-the-People Session last night when the hon Member Vikram Nair had posed two questions to me and I hope to just have a quick minute to respond to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, he stated that I agreed with the proposal by the hon Member Leong Mun Wai that land cost should be separated and charged at the point of sale.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: Second, Mr Vikram Nair had also explained that the Bala's Curve was not an accurate description of the secondary market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: In fact, I fully agree and that is why I had included in my handout the alternative, which is where prices rise due to incorporating rental inflation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: But most crucially, that chart also shows how house prices can become unhinged as inflation rises, which was the thrust of my argument as well as my concern.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: On to Senior Minister of State Sim Ann's argument.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: Just to be clear, we are not dismissing the valuable benefits that accrue to those who choose to in fact own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: Besides capital gains, they can also enjoy the flexibility of interior design, which many Singaporeans do exercise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: But I think she would agree with me that there are also costs, principally, when one over-invests in housing and they forgo other potentially higher return assets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: Would Senior Minister of State Sim Ann argue that Singaporeans should thereby focus the vast majority of their retirement assets and hopes primarily on real estate?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second clarification has to do with the fact that I am glad she referred to my chart.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: It really warms my heart, just my heart.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: But notice that once we actually reach the 60 years or so, the only way to end up extracting the value is to sell it onto someone else so that we can actually retire comfortably by extracting that value.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: The question is, we are selling on a rapidly depreciating asset.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
text: What is the Government's plan, at least at the macro level, to prevent creating a generation of home purchasers who have bought at the tail end just before the music stops?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am also very heartened that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim brought up this point.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In fact, I really should have mentioned it earlier to thank him because he pointed out, indeed, that when flats reach the tail end of their leases, when you are talking about 20 years, 30 years left – you have made the point that it is very difficult to sell, is it not?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At that point in time, even if you had value, would the private market realise it for you?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is also the reason why I want to mention this because I really hope that Mr Leong Mun Wai can be fairer to VERS.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The benchmark with which he has judging SERS and VERS, but especially VERS, has been most unfair.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: You talked about whether or not having so much of our income used towards housing purchase, would that not free up our resources to do other pursuits?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think so, I think it would free up our resources to pursue things that we seek in lieu of the security that housing would bring in the first place.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is a very strange argument because it totally ignores the importance of housing towards building up financial security, retirement security – something that I was at some pains to share with the Member.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, if you did not have that, well, would you be doing other things?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: You sure would because you would be looking for other ways to make sure that you are able to deal with the vagaries of retirement life.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Surely, you will be pursuing ways to find other means of security; you will be concerned about how you are going to deal with your living expenses; you will be concerned about being set loose upon the rental market and so on and so forth.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Would you be doing a lot of things to maintain your security in such a situation?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for the point that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim made, the first point, about how you did the chart, I would also like to ask him a clarification.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: How does what he shared negate my basic point, which is that I recognise that his chart shows that value goes up and then eventually down?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The second point she asked was about whether I would acknowledge that the first part of the chart was actually high.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Yes, in fact, the very reason why I modelled the chart in that fashion was to try to capture the realities of the secondary market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The concern that I have is that we may be over inflating; and the last thing we want to do is to encourage a bubble to grow even further.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, being an economist, would understand the fungibility of assets and of resources.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And if a Singaporean was able to achieve financial security in the form of a home, you consider it perhaps over-investment, but when you have the home and you have the security, you have the options to monetise, is that not worth something?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And does that not in itself, also free you up for other pursuits?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In fact, I find this argument that because you are investing in homes you cannot do other things – I think that Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is turning a blind eye to the fact that actually, you do need to have the security; you need to have the options.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And I have also laid out all the options and that alone allows you to pursue many other things that you could not if you did not have housing security.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: My reply to Mr Leon Perera: I am glad for your interest in VERS.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I may have missed the point that she was making about HPI.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: She said any number below 5 looks attractive.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe this is what the Senior Minister of State had said.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm if she was referring to the resale prices, or to the BTO prices?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And if it referred to non-mature BTO prices?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am not quite clear when you say HPI below 5, which category of flats you are referring to – resale or BTO?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Actually, Leader of Opposition, I was referring to the points that I believe your Members have raised.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And they have, I believe, also raised an alternative target – instead of HPI 5 for non-mature estate BTO, how about HPI equals 3 for 4-room non-mature estate BTO.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I think, actually that basis came from your Members.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I asked the question because in 2013, Mr Khaw Boon Wan spoke of the HPI and wanting to ensure that the HPI comes down to 4.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That was why I was asking the question to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: When she said anything below 5 is affordable, is that a shift of the Government's position?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: She, however, also requested that she could sell her existing flat high in the resale market so that she could make more profit for her retirement.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, if you think further, someone will have to pick up the bill, the question is: who is going to pay for and bear the burden of the difference?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Ultimately, it is the taxpayers – our children, our grandchildren.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB flats have evolved to provide not only roofs over our heads but also to support retirement as part of our social safety net.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very much in support of the measures for retirees to support their retirement needs through the Lease Buyback Scheme and renting out of rooms as an option.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These are workable as there is a market premium.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are serious concerns if nobody will want to pay the market premiums for Singapore’s properties and HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Despite the availability of cheaper options even in other countries around Singapore, investors are willing to pay premiums for our properties as they have included other intrinsic values, such as social and home security, environmental friendliness, infrastructural convenience, supporting amenities and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are many factors that affect the prices of properties, but the main one is demand and supply.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, in tandem with our dynamic economic growth and generally optimistic outlook for our future development, the demand is strong.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, the value of our land and properties has risen correspondingly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For today’s debate, the focus is on HDB flats, which house about 80% of our resident population.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The land which HDB flats stand upon have increased in value.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB building quality and maintenance also help to hold their values vis-à-vis private properties.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The current policy that all land sale proceeds will have to return to our national reserves is a wise approach.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is fair that the premium and costs of the land sales are to be shared by all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would prevent the Government of the day from finding an easy way to finance the national expenditure.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, there is a risk that the Government would have less incentive to cool a rising property market if it relies on land sales to fund expenditures.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There will be other questions arising from there for the public and for the residents.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will there be allocation based on family size, based on standard sizes of flats and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In their Members' proposal, the result will be likely that there will not be any more resale market.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the Members propose to look after Singaporeans who want to age in place and also need cash for retirement as they are left with residual values of the construction cost?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Members have to address what will be a fair residual value and if it is a straight-line depreciation, or heavy front-load and light-back?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What about residents who want to right-size to smaller flats to monetise the value for retirement, and also to have smaller flats to maintain?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I heard the clarification by the hon Member that the residual value is required to pay back the land cost plus interest even when the person has departed.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think it is quite sad that even when the person has departed, payment is still required.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think it is good to avoid that.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The proposal to only consider the locations for the price differences in itself has clearly indicated that one has accepted that there is indeed a premium for land value, notwithstanding that there are premiums for other factors too.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We will be better able to address Singaporeans' concern and fear.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Furthermore, Singaporeans can use their CPF to service their mortgage without the need to pay, using cash or only using minimum cash outlay.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It has provided great support for most Singaporeans in the face of the challenging market currently.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the other hand, we need to guard against the price-gap between HDB prices and private property prices widening, and the Government continues to ensure that flats remain affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Ministry must be careful not to leave the prices of private housing unchecked.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is certainly unhealthy and worrying if HDB resale prices and private property prices are rising without fundamentals.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I understand there are also negative sales in the market.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Minister share what are the negative sales for each of the last five years, if data is available?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is no doubt of the need for us to continue our efforts to ensure affordable homes for Singaporeans and remain committed to our mission of homes for everyone “居者有其屋”.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We are not just building housing but also endearing homes for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I support the Motion by Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: When it comes to a topic like housing, something that has such a disproportionate impact on our lived experience and which holds so much of Singaporeans’ wealth, it is important to get the facts on the table and to flesh out the arguments rigorously, responsibly and grounded in reality.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We have had a broad subject before us and it has been a long debate.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I am going to focus on getting first-time buyers on the home ownership ladder.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I will start by reaffirming the importance of home ownership, before sharing my views on the present situation and some proposals for consideration.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And the idea that a city-state such as ours could achieve over 90% home ownership has been a great source of pride as a Singaporean abroad.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Home ownership allows people to settle down, to start families, to grow old, without the fear of having to move from place to place when the landlord wants to raise the rent.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Home ownership gives people something to be proud of, something they can make as an expression of their selves.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And home ownership provides ordinary Singaporeans, regardless of income or family background, the opportunity to build an asset and to build themselves up.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For HDB homes, home ownership provides the ultimate security, something to fall back on, the one thing that cannot be taken away even if you go bankrupt.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For all the above reasons, home ownership must remain not just the Singaporean dream, but the Singaporean reality.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But that reality appears to be challenged today.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Rising resale prices and rents have sparked debate about whether public housing is still affordable.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Housing related appeals make up a third of our weekly Meet-the People Sessions (MPS) case volume for me, and for many of my parliamentary colleagues.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There is genuine concern among young Singaporeans and their parents whether they will be able to afford a flat.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I hope that the Minister’s explanation of how HDB keeps BTOs affordable has reassured them.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Taken together, these three issues mean some people find they cannot get the flat they want, BTO or otherwise.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Allow me to say a little more about the BTO mix issue.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We are reaching the development limits in many areas, even in some non-mature estates, including in my own constituency, Woodlands.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We also have more BTO configurations to cater for, to more diverse needs, for example, the needs of seniors and singles.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: While 20,000 new BTO flats used to mean pretty close to 20,000 less expensive flats in non-mature estates, in the August 2022 launch, more than 60% of the 3- to 5-room flats on offer were in more expensive mature estates, including the PLH.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This creates the perception that BTOs are getting more expensive overall, when in fact BTO prices in non-mature estates have not gone up so much.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As the hon Member Mr Cheng Hsing Yao has eloquently explained, there is good reason why flats in mature estates cost more and to suppress BTO prices in these mature estates would create unfair windfall gains for a small group – a situation that HDB rightfully guards against, in setting BTO prices.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This shifting BTO mix has different implications for buyers who want to buy in a mature estate and those who want to buy in a non-mature estate.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For the first-time buyer who wants to buy a BTO in mature estates, they now have more choices, if they are prepared to pay the higher price.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The innovations in the PLH model provide a useful reference to explore more ways to make them more affordable.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For first-time buyers who want to buy a BTO in a non-mature estate, the supply is sometimes not as high as it used to be.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Many of my residents, first-time buyers but also second- or third-time buyers who come to see me at my Meet-the People Sessions want to stay in or near Woodlands.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It is cheaper, closer to their parents and support networks, and, dare I say, we have done a pretty good job of making Woodlands a nice place to live, with noticeable improvements in connectivity and amenities.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Some of my residents try again and again for BTO and Sales of Balance Flats.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: One couple told me they had applied 11 times, because they want to stay in or near Woodlands – that is their expectation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But resale has become too expensive for them, especially with the recent sharp rise in interest rates and lower loan values.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And even if they can afford it, when resale prices get so far away from BTO prices, it creates another issue.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Those who get BTOs can make huge profits when they sell, those who do not get BTOs have much less upside, even with all the grants.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In a debate on housing though, it can be difficult to distinguish between fact and opinion.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We have heard a lot of opinions and I will add my opinions to this.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And so, any proposal that ignores this fact or is cavalier about the trade-offs that ensue are really non-starters – lacking in rigour, responsibility and realism.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I listened carefully to the proposals presented by PSP and WP for significantly cheaper BTO prices.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I cannot help but feel a sense of disquiet at how they gloss over the potential disruption to the wealth of 1.1 million Singaporean families, families that comprise low-income, middle-income and affluent families.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I hope the PSP in particular, will clarify how they imagine the resale market will remain “buoyant” and address the need for people to upgrade or downgrade as their life circumstances changes, under their proposed affordable housing model.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But lest anyone think that I am somehow afraid to touch the resale market, quite the contrary.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I believe the resale market is part of the problem and has to be part of the solution.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And I also believe that the problems faced by the first-time buyers is not the problem of the first-time buyers alone.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There is a huge social benefit of housing and a huge social cost of housing delays – on fertility rates, on how well kids can focus and do in school, on productivity and mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In the kinder, gentler, more inclusive Singapore that so many of us have talked about in this House, these social costs will only result in more Government expenditure down the road.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Thus, in my vision for a new social compact, everyone in the housing market should be willing to play their part.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Home owners should not necessarily expect that the value of their flats will increase inexorably year after year because housing goes in cycles.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Landlords should not push to maximise their rents or prices at all costs.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Buyers should not be jumping into the BTO market when they do not really need a flat, just because they can.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And HDB should revisit the balance of financial costs and benefits of housing policies with the social and environmental costs and benefits.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The BTO model was created to prevent the supply overhang in the 1990s from being repeated.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And it has served us pretty well until recent times.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Prior to COVID-19, it was three to four years.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Yes, a three- to four-year wait was less than ideal for some, but the model largely was passable for most.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: HDB has also shown itself to be responsive to the needs of first-time buyers by introducing Short Waiting Time (SWT) flats, announced as early as 2017, albeit in small numbers.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: So, I do not believe the BTO model is fundamentally flawed, though I hope the waiting time can go down.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I have confidence that the building programme will bring the BTO market to pre-COVID-19 norms in the next couple of years.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I am also comforted to hear the Minister speak about building more SWT flats and over time, recalibrating its building programme so that SWT flats form a larger proportion of new flats.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But the problems we see today would still be there if another COVID-19 happens even if we had a lot more SQT flats.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: And contrary to the Member Ms Hazel Poa, I actually do not think it is quite so easy to predict demand, given the number and dynamism of the factors at play.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Further, as supply chains in other industries have learnt following the pandemic, there is a need to strengthen resilience against potential black swan events going forward.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: These Zero Waiting Time flats would increase the responsiveness of housing supply, which will help achieve better outcomes, including helping moderate housing prices, provide for population growth and improve choice.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This will allow cheaper flats while shifting the market a little further away from speculation, while helping to set price levels for flats of different tenures.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Next, unlocking the resale market, because the solution cannot and should not lie in building new flats alone.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: You cannot build flats fast enough to meet the demand in the short term, nor is it sustainable or an optimal use of resources for the long term.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: After all, our country is small, with many competing demands for our reserves, including land, and our population is ageing.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There will be more people dying every year, leaving behind empty flats.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The key to giving Singaporeans a chance to own homes that allow them to start a family today, not in five years' time, to live close to their parents and their support networks, not on the other side of the island, lies in unlocking the resale market, making it more affordable and accessible for Singaporeans not lucky enough to secure a suitable BTO flat for themselves.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There are a number of measures that could provide some immediate relief and I would like to share a couple today.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Today, HDB offers a number of grants to make resale housing affordable.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There is research though in other cities in the world that shows that subsidies tend to be capitalised in housing prices.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Hence, the benefit is captured by the owners, especially if housing demand is driven up by the subsidy scheme while housing supply is rather inelastic.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Personally, I have grappled with the merits of the subsidy and whether increasing them further would just drive higher prices and create more economic rent for owners.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But, Mr Speaker, if we look in our hearts, I think the need to get the first-time buyers a home should trump this.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Applied with the right limits, only for first-time buyers, only in areas with high BTO application rates and in concert with other levers to loosen supply, the price effect of subsidies could be more controlled.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As mentioned before, the Government has said that it is soliciting views on this as part of the Forward Singapore conversation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Given the state we are in, I urge the Government, to put in crudely, to hurry up.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Doing this would signal that public housing is primarily a place to live in.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Of which, 45% rent out the whole flat and another 4% rent out one or more bedrooms.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It is not a large number that would disrupt the market, but not insignificant relative to the number of first-time buyers.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Given the social benefit, this exercise could be sweetened by offering breaks on stamp duty for selling their HDB flat.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Another perhaps more palatable option, is to ban such owners from renting their flats, which would likely induce many of them to sell their flats at more reasonable prices.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Together with the cooling measures and the dissipation of induced demand as BTO projects are delivered, the suggestions above could increase resale supply and moderate resale prices, providing more opportunity for more first-time homebuyers to get the flat they want in the locations they want.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I have focused on first-time buyers in my speech because they are, rightly so, the first priority.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But I urge HDB to not declare victory when the first-time buyers are "settled".

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Look out for the other groups that face frictions in getting on, off and sometimes back on the housing ladder today – the non-traditional families, transnational or reconstituted families, the ex-offenders, the singles.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: HDB will also has to address the concerns of seniors in our ageing population, though here I think the range of options available including the Lease Buyback Scheme are quite comprehensive and should be further promoted.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It is not easy to meet the needs and aspirations of all, but I have full faith in the HDB that has the vision, the focus and the heart to do this.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: If we were going to get the people to take National Service seriously, I could not ask their sons to fight and die for the properties of the wealthy.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We worked out a personal savings scheme that allowed them to own an apartment painlessly through instalments over 20 years.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We sold the apartments to them at below cost to enhance their assets.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It has immeasurably increased their wealth and our social stability." It is uncanny how it remains true today.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Let us renew, therefore, our vision, our focus, and our hearts, so that current and future generations of Singaporeans will have the opportunity to own a home that enhances the dignity, well-being and wealth.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I support the Motion moved by the Minister for National Development.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, I rise in support and agree that public housing in Singapore is indeed affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: It is also an asset for many young Singaporeans, who either wish to live there for the foreseeable future until their lifestyle needs have shifted; or live there for the long term.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Accessibility to and ownership of a HDB flat is a key factor in determining whether young couples wish to settle down and start families in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The negative public sentiment against the rising cost of public housing is not new and has been there for some time and also the recent hike in resale prices.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This we know is mainly due to supply and demand for houses especially within the mature estates which are usually more popular.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is unfair to say that public housing is unaffordable as prices are determined through a negotiation process between sellers and buyers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, a valuation process is required by HDB for every sale to take place.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The sentiments on public housing varies based on the engagements that I have had with my fellow union leaders, members and workers.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Another concern to note is the quality of workmanship of the new BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This accords with the principle that we should live and spend within our means.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Practically, this also includes their choice of flat ranging between 2-room and 5-room flats, depending on the couple’s financial ability.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: If an individual’s choice of home in terms of size and location does not match their financial capability, it does not automatically mean that public housing is not affordable.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: My wife and I were hoping to stay near my in-laws in Toa Payoh when we married and wanted to settle down in 1999.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, prices in Toa Payoh were high considering it being a central location and popular estate.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We considered purchasing a new flat but the long waiting time deterred us from doing so.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: As such, we discussed and identified possible areas with 5-room flats within our financial means.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We finally set our roots in Yishun, which was just a 15-minue walk to near Northpoint.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In short, we got our 5-room within our means, accessible to many amenities and best of all, many primary and secondary schools, all within 10 minutes of walking distance.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We are also thankful for the grant extended to us, which was at that time was a mere $35,000.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We stayed in our matrimonial home for five years and have since moved a couple of times before settling down at our current jumbo-sized home in Woodlands.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This may or may not be my final residence as our needs change as we age and we may not need a large space in the future.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Over the course of the years, we had on certain occasions lost monies in particular transactions and profited at a later stage.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, on balance, we have earned some monies through the sale and purchase of our homes which will be used for our retirement.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This example is not just unique to me.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure there are many Singaporeans out there shared the same experience.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, I have heard of many, including my fellow Members, who have upgraded from public housing to staying in private apartments or even some landed homes.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: For the record, these are not necessarily high earners.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Some are even normal working people like myself with stable job and progressive income over the years.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate Mr Leong Mun Wai's efforts in providing a big breakdown of the amount required to own a new home yesterday.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: However, it will be more useful for Mr Leong and his team to, likewise, provide examples of fellow Singaporeans who have profited from the sale of their HDB for the purchase of private properties so that a more balanced view is canvassed.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Let us not take away the efforts of our fellow Singaporean policy makers in MND and HDB who monitor and review housing policies regularly with a view to making public housing affordable and accessible since our Independence till now and even in the future.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   I support the Motion on the affordability of public housing for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This will alleviate the burden of debt, and the price of the flat is discounted after deducting the grant amount.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Public housing should be made a priority for our people who can afford it and are eligible for ownership.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We should make use of the support provided by the various Government grants.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We must believe that the Government will always strive to make public housing affordable for all levels of society.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Individuals, couples and families must make their own financial calculations and assessments before opting to buy a house.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: If the location of our dreams is beyond our means, we should be open to searching and buying a house that we can afford.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: The journey towards public housing ownership requires time and planning.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Let us not take the easy way out and blame the policies without finding out what has been provided by the Government.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Be fair to those who have been working hard in MND and HDB, who are constantly monitoring and making changes to ensure that Singaporeans can afford their own homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Motion standing in the name of the Minister for National Development affirms the PAP Government's commitment to keep public housing affordable and accessible for Singaporeans while safeguarding the interests of current and future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In his opening speech yesterday, Minister Desmond Lee explained how we have done this and how we intend to continue doing so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The PSP's Motion, on the other hand, implies that our system does not deliver affordable or accessible housing and that it is somehow fundamentally flawed despite the fact that 90% of Singaporeans living in HDB flats own their own homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More importantly, the PSP proposal most certainly does not safeguard the interests of current or future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Allow an individual to buy a new flat at a user price that is set based on construction costs and a notional location premium.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have no idea because Mr Leong Mun Wai has not told us how this notional location premium will be calculated.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the individual stays in the same flat for his entire life, he only needs to pay this user price.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, if the individual were to sell his flat in the resale market after the Minimum Occupation Period (MOP), he would have to pay the land cost that HDB had recorded at the point of purchase along with some accrued interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Essentially, it is a prepaid rental scheme with an option to buy.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is why Mr Leong Mun Wai uses the phrase "user price" and not "purchase price" because he knows it is not ownership.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The PSP portrays it as cheap housing with no downsides.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This sounds too good to be true – and if something sounds too good to be true, then it is because it probably is; too good to be true, that is.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is to say, there is a catch that you have not been told about.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: No matter which way you look at it, PSP's proposal involves selling state land cheaply.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under their scheme, when the flats are disposed by HDB to the user in the first instance, no one pays for the land cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, the user gets to stay in a nice BTO in a nice location with nice amenities at a low price without paying for any land cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If he chooses to sell, then and only then, he has to pay for the land cost with some accrued interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The land cost is a cost recorded with HDB at the time he gets the flat, not the current value of the land at the point when he sells.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you give it away cheaply or at zero cost, someone still has to bear the cost of that land.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under Mr Leong Mun Wai's proposal, the BTO user does not have to pay for land value or bear any cost of the land until he chooses to sell it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, who is paying for the land for the duration that the user stays there?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What Mr Leong Mun Wai has not told you is – you all are paying for it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The cost is borne by all other Singaporeans – each of us, in this generation as well as our children and grandchildren.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And what is the price that you will pay?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This land belongs to all of us, Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the Government, our approach, in line with our values, as a people and as a nation, is that we must be good stewards of this land for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Think of a family that has several parcels of land inherited from their grandparents.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One of the family members, the steward, is put in charge to manage the land on behalf of the family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Would you expect the steward to give away any one of those parcels to a developer for free and to recover only part of the land cost later?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If he gives it away for free or sells it at a partial recovery price, then he is shortchanging the rest of the family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They would be deprived of the value of the land.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, if the steward sells the land for a fair market value and invests the sale proceeds, the family will have the benefit of the original sale proceeds as well as the income from those proceeds.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This income can then be used partially for expenditure and partially reinvested to help sustain both present and future members of the family for years to come.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Everybody understands this in the context of family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is exactly how we do it as the Singapore family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: State land and our reserves belong to all Singaporeans, present and future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is a precious shared resource we must protect.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government is the steward of state land for the whole Singapore family.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If we do, we would be shortchanging Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the land remains in Government hands, the Government has to use it for the public good and we do not have to charge land cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, when we sell the land, we charge for it because the Government loses the use of it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On this point, I would like to provide a clarification to what Mr Sitoh Yih Pin said in his speech yesterday.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The principle Mr Sitoh Yih Pin articulated is correct.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have to account for the value of land when the state disposes of it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, if the land is used for public infrastructure like hospitals and public schools, it remains in the possession of the state and no payment arises.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is because it remains in the possession of the state.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is the case for Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The land was not sold for a nominal fee.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, when we sell land, we do so at a fair market value.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When that happens, the physical asset – the land	– is converted into sale proceeds or a financial asset.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To preserve the value of the reserves, the land sales proceeds go back into our shared reserves and are reinvested by our investment entities to benefit both current and future generations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If we do not account for the fair value of land or give it away free or at an under-value, our reserves will shrink each time land is used for public housing.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This means that over time, we will have less funds available for crises.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over time, the NIRC will get smaller and over time, in order to make up for the smaller NIRC, we will need to raise more taxes more quickly to get more revenue.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Despite Mr Leong Mun Wai's claims that he is not raiding the reserves, his proposal does exactly that.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai's proposal implicitly acknowledges this because he concedes that you must pay for the land when you sell it and it must go back to the past reserves.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under his scheme, the BTO users get to enjoy the land without paying for it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So long as they are occupying the flat without paying for the land, that is a draw on our reserves.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they choose not to sell, our reserves will be reduced for the entire duration of that occupation, presumably 99 years, although Mr Leong Mun Wai has not said what the tenure will be.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a result, we would forgo the monies that we would have invested and the investment returns under our current system.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That means less NIRC for the budget every year.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When Mr Leong Mun Wai says his scheme is better than using Government subsidies, he is actually taking from the Reserves and to make up for what the NIRC cannot now fund, we would have to either raise taxes or cut spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the PSP model, those who choose not to sell their flats will enjoy a large subsidy at everyone else's expense.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those who choose to sell their flats will have to pay recorded land cost and accrued interest but with no subsidies or grants.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some may have to sell their flats not for capital gains but for other reasons such as to cater to new needs and changes to lifestyle.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the property market is down, they may have to sell at a price lower than the recorded land cost and would lose out.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the one million existing homeowners, you should consider what PSP's proposal means for you.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If you are a HDB owner today, you should think what PSP's proposal means for you.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Essentially, there will be a new precinct right next to you with flats of similar attributes but much cheaper.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Please consider what this might mean to your property value.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Also consider is it fair that by policy design, somebody else gets the same flat as you but at a much cheaper price.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The PSP's model of differing land cost upon resale kicks the can down the road for home buyers who may well be worse off for this.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under PSP's model, there are no grants and subsidies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When the user sells his flat, he would have to pay for the recorded land cost without the benefit of grants or subsidies and this could affect his net proceeds.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And the question is whether this would be sufficient to finance another home.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is unlike the current HDB home ownership model, which enables Singaporeans to own their flat at an affordable price and benefit from our overall economic growth when they subsequently monetise it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: BTO applicants should consider what PSP's proposal means for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: With much cheaper flats paid for by everybody else, many people will join the queue.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The chances of a successful ballot will be lower.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There will be longer waiting times and greater uncertainty.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some will not be able to get a flat at all.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Then, what do you do about those who cannot get onto the affordable housing scheme and have to turn to the resale market?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under PSP's proposal, there will be no Government grants.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They will definitely ask for much larger grants and where will that be funded from?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is also a real risk of destabilising the resale and property market.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: PSP has also been very unclear as to the legal nature of this scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The overall scheme is rental with an option to buy, but he has not clarified what the user gets at the point of disposition.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the point of disposition, meaning when the user gets it from HDB, does the user get legal title or just a right to occupy?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If it is just the right to occupy, then the person is not the owner.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You only become an owner when you pay for the land and that only happens when you sell the land.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In short, you only own when you sell.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Whereas under our current scheme, you are the owner from the time that you buy the flat.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On the other hand, if the individual gets legal title at the point of disposition, then it means that they are enjoying ownership without paying for it – at least until they sell.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a narrative that has been perpetuated by both PSP and WP.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Otherwise, why do you have to pay for the land when you sell?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And you have the ability, once you get the title, to transfer that title; which you do not, if you are a mere tenant.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong said yesterday, "Singaporeans should be treated like citizens, not consumers." We believe Singaporeans should be treated like home owners, not users.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong had said that land cost should be taken out of the pricing of HDB flats.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas, earlier today, pointed out that this scheme puts land costs squarely in the midst of the pricing of HDB flats.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Of course, Mr Leong did stand up to clarify and said that as part of his "brilliant military strategy", he did not say earlier that this was related to owner-occupation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But then, what about the person who is buying from the erstwhile user?

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Land cost is right smack in the middle of the price that he is paying, and certainly, on all the social media posts, the impression that was created, not just to Mr Raj, but to all Singaporeans was that there was this wonderful scheme that would allow you to own without having to pay land cost.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Well, Mr Leong has now clarified it, but it would be good to tell people that what you are really selling them is a scheme to rent, not to own, and they will only own it as soon as they sell it and dispose of it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: PSP criticises the waiting times for BTO flats, yet, as I have explained, their proposal will add to the queues.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He has said that his proposal will not raid the reserves, but it is clear that it will.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He also said yesterday, that under his scheme, Singaporeans can look forward to a future when, I quote, "owner-occupied public housing is truly affordable, as land cost is waived." The irony is that for so long as you are occupying it, you are not the owner.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You only become the owner for just a short while before you sell it.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just a quick clarification for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann on VERS, as I took some time to relook at what has been shared so far in the public space.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I think Senior Minister of State spoke about how the Government under VERS would be the buyer of last resort.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Do Singaporeans have access to affordable public housing?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Has Singapore's public housing policies enabled Singapore Citizens, especially in the lower middle-income group, to own their own homes?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: So, I must thank the hon Member Mr Leong Mun Wai for putting up the Motion because it then gave me the motivation to go find out the outcomes.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number two: housing is usually the highest expenditure for any household.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mortgage service rate, or MSR, refers to the proportion of a borrower's gross monthly income that goes towards mortgage repayments for the HDB flat, and is a good benchmark for affordability.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: By global comparison, Singapore's MSR of 25% or lower is below the international benchmark of 30% to 35%, which indicates that public housing in Singapore is more affordable than elsewhere.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number three: moreover, given that for employees aged 55 years and below, employee and employer CPF contributions amount to 20% and 17% of employee income respectively, totaling 37% of income.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: So, for the buyers with MSR of 25% or lower, they can service their HDB loans using their monthly CPF contributions, with little or no cash outlay.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This is remarkably lower than the median price-to-income ratios in cities, like Hong Kong at 30.8, Beijing at 26.8, Shanghai at 24.5, Seoul at 18.6 and Tokyo at 16.6.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number five: in most parts of the world, affordable housing usually refers to low-income housing.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: But for us in Singapore, our affordable housing wins international accolades and awards for providing well-designed flats and high-quality living environments that is green, liveable and sustainable, and have the greatest effect on the people who use them each day.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number six: a study on International Housing Affordability Survey 2020 recognised the Singapore Government for heavily investing in the upgrading and renewal of HDB neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This helps to forestall urban decay, they wrote, in older areas and allows homeowners of all income levels a quality living environment comparable to newer neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number seven: HDB housing is referred to locally as public housing.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, unlike other public housing programmes, HDB flats are owned under 99-year leases by purchasers who are able to sell their units after a Minimum Occupancy Period (MOP) of five years, or 10 years for the Prime Location Public Housing (PLH) model, resale of HDB flats help to unlock the value of the HDB flats for many Singaporeans over the years, facilitating social mobility for HDB dwellers to upgrade to larger units, or to private housing even.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Outcome number eight: as Singaporeans move into the retirement phase, they are supported by the HDB Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) and the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) scheme, which allows the seniors to monetise their HDB flat while still living in it, or to monetise their HDB flat in the resale market and move into a smaller unit, with a shorter lease.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: In their golden days, they continue to have a home to age in place and have cash to support their retirement needs.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: How would you answer the two questions I posed at the start?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: What Singapore has achieved is truly a miracle and, definitely, not by accident.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Our leaders and our pioneering generation dared to dream together of the possibility of a metropolis rising out of a mudflat swamp and they worked together to make it happen, one brick at a time.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We are blessed that the successive generation of leaders in our Government continue to build on that dream and bring us to where we are today.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: There are many economists and governments studying the Singapore model and lessons learnt.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I quote from the Demographia International Housing Affordability Survey, 2020 edition: "no major metropolitan area in the high-income world faces the housing affordability challenge of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's six million people live on a fully developed island nation so small, that they could fit into one-half of Tokyo Bay.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: As a result, Singapore lacks the supply vent of low-cost suburban or exurban land that moderates house prices across an urban area.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This is Singapore's unequaled housing challenge... but Singapore has effectively managed its scarce land supply and established a market that produces middle-income housing affordability.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: HDB also seeks to achieve social objectives through its policies, such as to: promote progressivity by giving a higher grant amount to the lower income; promote family formation by providing bigger grant amounts for families than for singles; promote mutual care and support by encouraging families to live with or close to their parents or children.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The lesson of Singapore for the world is not so much the intricacies of its housing market design.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Rather, it is that Singapore pro-actively and successfully prioritized affordable home ownership for its citizens, and developed means to accomplish that objective based upon its unique conditions." Kudos to colleagues at MND, HDB, CPF and the whole-of-Government, for all that you do to house Singaporeans from cradle to retirement.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The paradigm shifts all the time and the COVID-19 pandemic has thrown quite a few curveballs at us from many directions and public housing is not precluded.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Over these past two days, many ideas have been thrown around and indulge me as I add a few to the already long list.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And as Minister Desmond shared yesterday, HDB is ramping up the construction of flats to catch up on lost time caused by COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, the key question is, what would it take for HDB to further ramp up the numbers and reduce the median wait time by half, to address the backlog and demand from, especially, the first-time applicants.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Meanwhile, I hear from a young couple that the interim rentals HDB offered for young families to set up home while waiting for the HDB keys have been most helpful.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: They are very grateful for HDB supporting them in their journey and more can benefit from this.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And of course, four in 10 applications reject when offered a flat, and perhaps that is why the supply demand forecasting is a little bit in the air.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This issue has to be managed, so that HDB can better plan demand and supply and I ask applicants: be serious, $10 for one application, that is why four in 10 applications reject.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Challenge number two: perception that BTO flat prices are unaffordable.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: From what I have seen, Singapore public housing is higher quality and more affordable than most other cities.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Affordability, as my fellow Nominated Member colleague said just now, is all about buying within your budget.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: This explains the big deficit that HDB chalks up every year for its Home Ownership Programme.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
